answer: A new agent should not get full trust at the dawn of its first job. Give it a slow horizon instead: it starts on tiny, low-value tasks, and its spending limit only rises after a string of completed work. Its record carries an umber badge that fades when it goes idle or misbehaves, and a small stake it posted gets slashed on fraud. Spinning up a thousand fresh identities then buys nothing, because each one still has to earn its way up, one job at a time.
